fatal_errors: The proposed material is an unspecified Fe-Cr-Ni-Co HEA rather than the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with its defining L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The stated 500 °C test temperature, 0.1 MPa contact pressure, and 10 Hz frequency are invented and conflict with the actual 25–100 °C, 5–15 N, and 3–9 Hz conditions.
The hypothesis confuses transient thermal-shock cycling to approximately 1100 °C with elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion service.
The proposed 30% degradation reduction is unsupported and misses the observed approximately order-of-magnitude wear-rate advantage.
The baseline is incorrectly specified as 316L stainless steel rather than identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205.
No evidence supports the asserted Cr2O3 composition or the quantitative prediction.
explanation: The response captures only the broad idea that a Cr-containing HEA may outperform a conventional alloy through protective passivation and reduced friction. It does not identify the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy, reconstruct the thermal-shock and immersed reciprocating test, or describe the retained L12/B2 lamellae, temperature-dependent wear regimes, and comparison with DS2205. Its experimental proposal is falsifiable in a generic sense, but the material, conditions, baseline, mechanism, and numerical threshold are insufficiently specified or unsupported.
